participation.$rosterNote: Committees are CONSTITUTED, not just volunteered for: bylaws set a minimum and a chair does not run a committee of one. The volunteer draw alone left 7 of 35 committee-terms below three members — the early years and the newly-formed committees, where the eligible pool was smallest. Short terms are topped up from the most engaged eligible members who are not already serving, which strengthens rather than weakens the engagement arrow.
participation.$note: share of term-start-covered members who serve on a committee; engaged members volunteer (theta arrow). ESTIMATE (confidence: low, researched 2026-07-16 - no direct published benchmark exists): consistent with ASAE Foundation's Decision to Volunteer study (Gazley & Dignam 2008, 26,305 respondents) finding 30% of members have EVER volunteered in any capacity - current committee service is a small subset of that. MGI benchmarking reports publish no members-on-committees share.
participation.$continuityNote: Rosters used to be wiped clean every term — 4% carryover, where real committees run 50-70% with staggered seats. Incumbency enters the volunteer score, so serving members are far likelier to serve again, and a returning member usually returns to the SAME committee. childOutcome still calibrates to shareOfEligible, so total participation is unchanged; only WHO fills the seats becomes continuous. ESTIMATE (confidence: low) — no published association committee-continuity benchmark found; 2.3 was chosen to land carryover in the 45-65% band.

meetings.$upcomingNote: committees schedule ahead — each carries this many future (Status Scheduled) meetings past the release so the app's 'upcoming meetings' view is populated; future meetings have no attendance/motions yet

attendance.$note: SOURCED 2026-07-16 (confidence: medium-high): governance-industry bands put >80% = strong, 70-80% = moderate, <70% = problem (kpidepot.com board-meeting-attendance-rate; boardeffect.com attendance trends); the SEC/public-company norm is directors attending >=75% of board+committee meetings (lexology.com 75%-attendance-test). 75% +/-6 spans the moderate band to the strong threshold.

motions.$contentiousNote: a share of motions are contentious — a tighter/against split so some genuinely FAIL. Outcome stays causally derived from the tally (yes>no), never forced; this just makes governance look real instead of rubber-stamp.
motions.$note: votes are CONSISTENT with attendance by construction — members absent from the meeting vote 'Absent'
topics: Form a working group on member feedback

committees.$historyNote: Governance used to start in 2023 while the committees claim formation dates from 2014-2017 — eight years of missing history, so every roster looked newly minted and no committee had a past. Terms now run biennially from 2015. Each term owns its own per-person stream (committee-serve:<member>:<termStart>) and its own meeting slots, so back-filling is ADDITIVE: the 2023-24 and 2025-26 terms and everything derived from them are untouched. A committee only gets terms after it was formed.
